Team — preliminary econ attached (Redwood_Competitive_Offer_2026.xlsx). High level notes:

- Anchors: Vendor X is currently offering an effective $0.0009 per token at 100M/mo with a 12-month commit. Their listed ‘migration credit’ is effectively a front-loaded 3-month credit.
- Our competitive posture: offer a 6-week pilot credit (~$25k compute credit), followed by a hybrid incentive: 3 months of graduated consumption credits + a volume rebate at 3 tiers (>=50M, >=150M, >=300M).
- Differentiators we must call out: superior latency SLO on our dedicated pools (p99 numbers), built-in fallback routing to cheaper model variants (configurable by route), and explicit KV/prefix caching that reduces billed tokens for repeated queries.

Proposed pricing sketch (see sheet "offer_summary"):
- Pilot: $25k compute credit + 2 free onboarding sprints (up to 40 engineering hours)
- Year 1 list rates: token/unit pricing slightly below Vendor X at the 100M and 200M tiers after rebate application
- Egress: we propose to absorb first 10TB egress during migration window or offer egress credits as part of pilot.

Open questions for Karthik: can we commit to p99 latency SLA at 300ms for their production routes if we put them on Dedicated? If not, we should hedge.

-jordan

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Quick tech/ops readout for the offer:

- Migration scope: 3 phases — pilot verification (non-prod), staged replay + data migration, production cutover. Expected engineering support: ~120 engineer-hours for full lift (integration + runbook + playbooks). Bootstrapping for AtlasMedic's custom prompt pipeline (composite prompts + function/tool calls) may add another 40 hours.
- Constraints: If AtlasMedic uses Vendor X's proprietary model variants, we need to validate compatibility; quantization differences may require retraining or model conversion for parity on p99 latency.
- SLA feasibility: We can commit to a p99 <= 300ms target on Dedicated for standard generation workloads if they accept a 99.5% availability SLA and limited burst allowance; we should include a fallback policy that routes to a slightly cheaper model variant automatically when Dedicated pool is saturated. This preserves availability but may affect per-token quality by a small, measurable margin.

I'll supply a short risk table and a conservative hours-by-phase that Grace can include in the mutual action plan.

-Karthik

Asha / team — thanks for the patience. Attached is our competitive offer and a short mutual-action plan for pilot -> production (see attachments and HubSpot link below). Highlights below: 

Offer highlights:
- Pilot package: $25k compute credit, 2 onboarding sprints (up to 40 engineering hours), and 10TB egress credit during migration window. Pilot term: 3 months.
- Pricing & rebates (year 1): Tiered volume rebate applied monthly at billing close. Effective post-rebate price targets are competitive with Vendor X at 100M and 200M token buckets. See sheet "offer_summary" for the math.
- Migration support: Redwood will provide a migration runbook, prioritized issue triage during cutover, and a dedicated technical onboarding lead for the first 6 weeks. We estimate ~160 engineer-hours to full production (see Karthik's phase breakdown).
- SLA & fallbacks: We can commit to p99 <= 300ms on Dedicated with a 99.5% availability SLA for the prioritized routes. In the event of sustained saturation, we will auto-route to a designated lower-cost model variant (customer-configurable) — this will be explicitly described in the mutual action plan and the fall-through quality delta measured on a small prompt set.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached proposal and mutual action plan.
2) If acceptable, sign the pilot addendum and we'll provision the pilot environment within 5 business days of DocuSign completion. DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/LA-12345-AtlasMedic-Redwood
3) Kickoff onboarding with Grace once DocuSigned.
